title: Indigenous-themed names policy and community grants approved
subtitle: Downtown Elora traffic study, Fergus rezoning, hospital staff housing lease, stormwater by-law and land debenture also approved.
overview: Council adopted a policy on Indigenous-themed names, logos and images in Township facilities. It also approved a permanent contextual display at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre, where historic lacrosse banners can be reinstalled. Council then approved 2026 Community Investment Fund grants, including four requests that go beyond the usual funding limit.

Council approved a zoning change for infill housing at 73 and 79 Sideroad 19 in Fergus. It directed staff to seek proposals for a Downtown Elora traffic study, with the Township paying its share alongside Wellington County. It also approved a lease with Groves Memorial Community Hospital for Craighead Cottage, to house recruited healthcare professionals.

Council authorized a by-law regulating activity in and around stormwater management facilities {{vote:m7}}. It also authorized a debenture by-law for borrowing to cover two land purchases, near the Sportsplex and the Middlebrook well site {{vote:m11}}. Fees and charges were amended, and staff said paid parking will probably start in spring. A closed session on Ontario Land Tribunal matters had nothing to report.

decisions.detail: Council adopted a policy on Indigenous-themed names, logos and images in Township facilities and directed staff to proceed with the permanent contextual display at the Jefferson Elora Community Centre.
Council approved the 2026 grant allocations recommended by the advisory committees, including the special considerations above the usual limit.
Council approved the zoning amendment for 73 and 79 Sideroad 19 and gave the by-law three readings.
Staff will issue a request for proposals for the study, and council approved the Township's share of funding alongside Wellington County.
Council authorized a lease with Groves Memorial Community Hospital for 495 Union Street West to house healthcare professionals being recruited, with staff able to make minor amendments.
Council amended the 2026 Fees and Charges By-law to enact specific changes made since it was first passed.

debate: On the Downtown Elora traffic study, one councillor questioned why the Township would fund a study just after the budget was set and shortly after the County's fall study. They asked whether the County's pending changes should be given time to work first, and whether staff had capacity.

Supporters of the traffic study said the problem covers the whole downtown core, not one intersection. They said the County was willing to partner, with the Township leading. Staff said the scope covers the main routes and feeder streets, that active transportation options are not ruled out, and that capacity exists. Costs of any recommendations would come back to council.

On the Indigenous-themed names policy, councillors praised the collaborative working group. They suggested a similar display in the Fergus arena, where lacrosse is also played, and asked about a piece of the artwork for the council chamber. Staff said the artist's statement will be displayed at eye level beside the QR code.

On the Community Investment Fund, councillors asked why applications fell in two streams. Staff cited volunteer turnover at groups, missed email notices and a long application timeline, and said they are looking at tightening the process. Staff also explained that stacking funding is discouraged, not prohibited.

On the Fergus rezoning, a councillor asked where residents would store the new large recycling carts. Staff said garbage collection would be per property, and that the County's waste services would settle arrangements at the later condominium stage.
